data_as_of: Futures, VIX, 10Y, DXY, oil, gold, BTC: Yahoo v7 quotes ~7:34–7:49 a.m. CT. Stock and ETF pre-market prices and volumes: StockAnalysis quote API ~7:50 a.m. CT, cross-checked against Yahoo's screener (~7:45 a.m. CT). Cash closes are Tuesday Oct 13.
headline: A hotter-than-expected September CPI (3.7% vs 3.6%) has futures lower, with Russell 2000 futures down 1.1%, while Bank of America falls 7% on a $1.2B penalty-driven miss and Liquidia jumps 37% on a litigation settlement.
notes: Scheduled run at ~7:49 a.m. CT, before the 8:30 a.m. CT open: PRE-MARKET. All movers use live pre-market data dated Oct 14 (StockAnalysis and Yahoo via the Mac browser). CPI was released at 7:30 a.m. CT, so futures and yields reflect it.

Gap % = pre-market price vs Tuesday's close (StockAnalysis). Quality movers were screened from Yahoo's US list of stocks ≥$5 and ≥$2B (top 3,000 by market cap; 1,136 had an Oct 14 pre-market quote) and confirmed on StockAnalysis. LQDA ($2.40B) was missing from Yahoo's top-3,000 pass and was added from StockAnalysis.

Excluded as data artifacts: SKYD (Yahoo −16%, StockAnalysis +64% on 3.7K shares; shares began trading without warrant entitlement, so prior-close bases differ), BMO and RY (Yahoo +4.5–4.9% vs StockAnalysis −0.4–0.7% on a few hundred shares), NICE (Yahoo −6% vs StockAnalysis −0.6% on 826 shares).

Names with <10K pre-market shares were left out of the movers tables as too thinly traded: ESLT (+6.2%, 4K), EAT (+2.8%, 3K), SHG (−4.3%), and several quotes with no pre-market volume (LYV, GPN, FERG, EXR). VIR (+9.4%, Gilead collaboration) is $1.8B market cap, below the $2B cutoff.
Relative volume = pre-market volume ÷ 3-month average full-day volume (Yahoo), so values are naturally small before the open.

Gap watchlist: LQDA's settlement is not a listed catalyst type by itself; it was kept because BTIG upgraded it to Buy the same morning. CRWV, NBIS, IONQ, WULF, CRDO and VAL were excluded for no company-specific catalyst of a listed type. DELL (−3.84%) is close to the threshold.
CNBC's CPI article could not be fetched (WebFetch error), so CPI figures come from Yahoo Finance's live blog. Core CPI month-over-month was not found.

Under-$5 lists are StockAnalysis's top-20 pre-market gainers and losers (~7:50 a.m. CT), filtered to ≥100K shares and <$5. Market cap is StockAnalysis's figure (based on the prior close). Float was not available, and reverse-split history was not checked. AEHL (+178%, $23.74, ~$12M cap) and GRML (+42%, $7.85, Greenland theme) fit neither table.
Mortgage applications and Beige Book times are their usual 7 a.m. and 2 p.m. ET schedule, not confirmed today.
drivers: September CPI came in hot: headline rose 3.7% year over year versus 3.6% expected (0.6% month over month, in line), and core rose 2.6% versus 2.5%, driven by gas and energy. Futures turned lower after the print: S&P 500 −0.3%, Nasdaq-100 −0.6% and Russell 2000 −1.1%, while the 10-year yield rose 6 bp to 5.27% and the dollar firmed. Fed officials are leaning hawkish: New York Fed President Williams sees one more hike as appropriate this year and Boston's Collins wants another; CME FedWatch still shows ~78% odds of a hold at the next meeting. Oil is up 1.6% (WTI $95.63; Brent above $105) as Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities continue, and gold is down 1.1%. Korean stocks rebounded after a 12% five-day KOSPI slide; ASML posted record Q3 sales and raised its outlook but trades −1.3%. Bank results are mixed: Bank of America −7% after a $1.2B money-laundering penalty drove an EPS miss, State Street −8.7% on a revenue miss, Morgan Stanley −2.4% despite beating on equity trading, and BlackRock +2.3% on a beat. Barclays downgraded HPE, Dell and NetApp, citing no meaningful enterprise AI inflection yet.
